title: The Garden of the Weeping Wood
premise: In the city of Corvale, where magic was outlawed after the Sundering, Wren Thornbury has survived seven years as a debt-bound scribe selling harmless charms—until the old gods begin answering prayers again and her own small magic flares into something undeniable. Hunted by the Inquisitors' Office and bound by a debt she cannot pay, Wren discovers she is the last heir of the Weeping Wood, the grove where gods and mortals once sealed their covenant. To reforge it, she must ally with an exiled god who may be lying to her, betray or redeem the mentor who sold her into debt, and choose between the law that kept the city safe and the truth of why the covenant broke. In the end, Wren renews the covenant not by restoring the old order but by rewriting its terms—making magic answerable to mortals—at the cost of her own name in the city's records, freeing her from debt by erasing the life that owed it.
about_author: Odile Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed folk charms before turning to fiction. She writes from a cottage full of unlabeled seed jars and insists the garden names them for her.

chapters.title: The Price of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the market of Corvale, Wren sells a luck-charm to a desperate mother while hiding her debt-brand beneath her sleeve. When the charm actually works—impossibly—the mother weeps, and Wren feels the old power stir. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; the first crack in seven years of careful smallness.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Summoned to the Scriptorium, Wren learns her debt has been bought by a stranger's seal. Her mentor, Magister Halev, warns her to stop selling charms before the Inquisitors notice. That night, a prayer whispered over her counter is answered aloud. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the walls of her careful life closing in.

chapters.title: What the Gods Remember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the answered prayer to a ruined shrine, Wren meets Ashen-Vey, an exiled god wearing a beggar's body, who claims her blood opened the way back. He tells her the covenant of the Weeping Wood can be reforged—but only by its lost heir. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity; the past claiming her.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Marrec's POV. Marrec investigates the working charm, genuinely sympathetic to the poor but bound to enforce the ban that ended the Godswar. He traces the signature to the Scriptorium's ledgers. Emotional beat: duty as devotion; a good man sharpening toward a bad act.

chapters.title: Seven Years Owed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fleeing the shrine raid, Wren confronts Halev and learns he sold her into debt years ago to protect her—and has now sold her location to buy time. Betrayed, she flees with Ashen-Vey through the undercity. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve; loyalty questioned at its root.

chapters.title: Beneath the Bellows Street
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the smuggler warrens, Wren finds an underground congregation of hidden believers who have prayed to silence for a generation. Their elder recognizes the Thornbury name and gives her her grandmother's covenant-token. Emotional beat: belonging offered by strangers; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Law of Ash
chapters.summary: Marrec's POV. Marrec interrogates Halev and uncovers the truth of the Sundering's official history—that the ban was built on a forged account of the Godswar. Ordered to destroy the evidence, he keeps one page instead. Emotional beat: the first splinter in certainty.

chapters.title: Road Through the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Ashen-Vey travel to the petrified grove at the city's edge, where trees weep sap like tears. The grove tests her with visions of her grandmother sealing the covenant—and of the gods breaking faith first. Emotional beat: the seduction and danger of inherited purpose.

chapters.title: Terms of the Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Ashen-Vey's POV. The god confesses a fraction of his exile: he argued for mercy during the Godswar and was cast down for it. He needs Wren not only as heir but as anchor—a mortal vessel to hold divine power. Emotional beat: tenderness braided with manipulation; love as leverage.

chapters.title: A Charm Against Forgetting
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Back in Corvale to gather allies, Wren finds the underground congregation arrested. She frees them using magic she barely controls, and the city sees. Rumor spreads like fire: the gods are awake. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; no more hiding.

chapters.title: The Debt Called Due
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Halev, dying of the price he paid for his bargains, asks Wren's forgiveness and gives her the original covenant terms—which name a mortal veto the gods never honored. She forgives him, but does not absolve the system that made him sell her. Emotional beat: complicated mercy; truth over loyalty.

chapters.title: Marrec's Choice
chapters.summary: Marrec's POV. Ordered to execute captured believers, Marrec refuses publicly, burning his commission and the forged history page in the plaza. Arrested, he sends word to Wren: he knows how the Inquisitors plan to end the awakening—by burning the Weeping Wood itself. Emotional beat: conscience outranking law.

chapters.title: What the Fire Wants
chapters.summary: Ashen-Vey's POV. Ashen-Vey urges Wren to let the grove burn—it would free the gods from mortal constraint entirely, unbound and vengeful. Wren realizes his mercy in the Godswar was strategic, not moral. Emotional beat: betrayal within intimacy; seeing the beloved clearly.

chapters.title: The Gathering of the Small Faithful
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren rallies freed believers, deserting soldiers, and even charm-buyers from her market days—an army of the overlooked. They march for the grove ahead of the Inquisitors' pyre-wagons. Emotional beat: ordinary people choosing; belonging forged, not found.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Watch
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the eve of battle, Wren visits Marrec in his cell; they argue law versus justice and part as something like friends. Ashen-Vey offers her escape; she refuses. Emotional beat: stillness before storm; every relationship weighed.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Grove
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Inquisitors fire the Weeping Wood. Wren walks into the flames to reach the heart-tree, shielded by believers who die holding the line. The grove's dying magic floods her with every prayer ever unanswered there. Emotional beat: sacrifice; grief as fuel.

chapters.title: Heir of the Heart-Tree
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the charred heart-tree, Wren stands between Ashen-Vey and the arriving god-host, and invokes the covenant's forgotten mortal veto. The gods must hear terms or lose the last door back to the world. Emotional beat: a debt-bound scribe out-lawyering the divine.

chapters.title: Terms Renegotiated
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren dictates new covenant terms: magic answers prayers by consent, gods walk bounded by witness, and mortals keep the veto. Ashen-Vey, offered freedom without power, chooses to stay bound beside her—his first honest choice. Emotional beat: hard-won justice outside any lawbook.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Names
chapters.summary: Marrec's POV. Freed and reinstated by a changed Office—or resigning to join the new Order of Witness—Marrec presides over the public reading of the true history. Halev's name is cleared posthumously; Wren's debt-record is read aloud and annulled. Emotional beat: public truth as restitution.

chapters.title: Sap and Seedling
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Spring comes to the burned grove; green shoots rise through ash. Wren plants her grandmother's token at the heart-tree and takes up work as the covenant's first Witness-scribe, writing prayers down so none go unheard again. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into tending.

chapters.title: The City That Learned to Pray Aloud
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Market day in a changed Corvale: charms sold openly, an Inquisitor-turned-Witness hearing grievances, children leaving offerings. Old fears linger in some quarters, and the new covenant is tested by a petty dispute handled fairly. Emotional beat: fragile, imperfect peace taking root.

chapters.title: The Garden Tends Its Gardener
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Years later, Wren walks the grown Weeping Wood with Ashen-Vey, now merely strange rather than divine. A young debt-bound scribe arrives seeking help, echoing Wren's old life, and Wren opens the door wide. Emotional beat: the arc closed and handed on; belonging finally, freely chosen.
